intro: The Pediatric Appendicitis Score (PAS) is a GI & Liver scoring tool used in paediatric practice. Likelihood of acute appendicitis in a child with abdominal pain. It scores 8 criteria and interprets the total across 3 bands, so the number always arrives with the severity it implies rather than on its own. In PediAid each criterion is shown as a labelled option with the weight it carries, so the total can be checked rather than taken on trust.
indications: Grading severity at the bedside in GI & Liver
Recording an objective severity band in the case notes
Deciding when a total crosses the threshold for escalation
Re-scoring to track whether a child is improving or deteriorating
Checking the exact criteria of a score used infrequently
method: The score sums 8 criteria: Cough / percussion / hopping tenderness in RLQ; Right lower quadrant tenderness; Anorexia; Pyrexia ≥ 38 °C; Nausea or vomiting; Migration of pain to RLQ; Leucocytosis ≥ 10 000 /µL; Neutrophilia ≥ 7 500 /µL. Totals are then banded: any score - Low risk: pAS ≤3 - appendicitis unlikely. Consider discharge with review, or observation if the story is atypical; 4 points or more - Equivocal: pAS 4-6 - equivocal. Imaging (ultrasound first in children) and/or serial examination with surgical input; 7 points or more - High risk: pAS ≥7 - appendicitis likely. Surgical referral; many centres proceed without further imaging.
guidelineRefs: Source: Samuel M. Pediatric appendicitis score. J Pediatr Surg 2002;37:877-81.

faqs.q: How many criteria does the Pediatric Appendicitis Score (PAS) use?
faqs.a: 8. They are Cough / percussion / hopping tenderness in RLQ; Right lower quadrant tenderness; Anorexia; Pyrexia ≥ 38 °C; Nausea or vomiting; Migration of pain to RLQ; and others.

faqs.q: What do the bands of the Pediatric Appendicitis Score (PAS) mean?
faqs.a: The total is interpreted as: any score - Low risk: pAS ≤3 - appendicitis unlikely. Consider discharge with review, or observation if the story is atypical; 4 points or more - Equivocal: pAS 4-6 - equivocal. Imaging (ultrasound first in children) and/or serial examination with surgical input; 7 points or more - High risk: pAS ≥7 - appendicitis likely. Surgical referral; many centres proceed without further imaging.

faqs.q: Does the score replace clinical judgement?
faqs.a: No. It is a structured way to record and communicate severity. A clinician concerned about a child should act on that concern regardless of the total.

faqs.q: Where does this score come from?

faqs.a: Yes. Score definitions are bundled with the PediAid app, so the score computes without a connection.
